label: Plot
description: One plotline, main plot or subplot, from the disturbance that sets it moving, through its complications and climax, to its resolution. It follows the owner's goal, not single dated events or any character's inner life.

fields.label: Plotline owner
fields.help: The character whose decisions drive this plotline forward and whose goal it follows.

fields.label: Weight in the book
fields.help: How much of the book this plotline carries compared with the other plotlines.

fields.label: Opening disturbance
fields.help: The event that breaks the owner's starting situation and forces this plotline into motion.

fields.label: Driving goal
fields.help: What the owner sets out to achieve in response to the disturbance, stated as something that can be won or lost.

fields.label: Opposing force
fields.help: Who or what works against the owner's goal within this plotline, whether a person, a group, a place or a circumstance.

fields.label: Complications
fields.help: The obstacles and reversals the owner meets, one per item in story order, each making the goal harder to reach.

fields.label: Pace of escalation
fields.help: How steeply the pressure on the owner rises from one complication to the next.

fields.label: Climax
fields.help: The decisive confrontation in which the owner's goal is finally won or lost, and what the owner does there.

fields.label: Outcome of the goal
fields.help: Where the climax leaves the driving goal, judged against what the owner set out to achieve.

fields.label: Resolution
fields.help: What is settled after the climax, how the owner's situation has changed because of it, and anything left deliberately open.

fields.label: Setups and payoffs
fields.help: Details this plotline plants early that must pay off later, each item naming the setup and where it pays off.

fields.label: Span in the book
fields.help: Where in the manuscript this plotline begins and ends, by part, act or chapter, and whether it runs throughout.

fields.label: How they fit together
fields.help: What each contributes to the other, and how the part sits within the whole.

fields.label: What sets them apart
fields.help: What one holds that the other lacks, so that the two never blur together.

fields.label: How one leads to the other
fields.help: The chain from the first to the second: what makes the second follow from it, rather than merely come after it.

fields.label: What the reader sees of the link
fields.help: Whether the reader notices the connection as it happens, later on, or only when looking back.

fields.label: What lies between them
fields.help: What happens, or is deliberately left out, between the first and the second.

fields.label: What holds it together
fields.help: Why this link exists: the need, duty, fear, belief or bargain that keeps it in place.

fields.label: What each side gives and gets
fields.help: What passes between the two because of this link, such as loyalty, protection, money, secrets or obedience.

fields.label: Where it strains
fields.help: The pressure that could break or turn this link, and what would follow if it gave way.

fields.label: How it changes
fields.help: Where this link stands at the start of the book and at its end, and what moves it.

fields.label: How it shows on the page
fields.help: Where and how the reader meets this link: in an action, an image, a setting or a choice.

fields.label: Why it matters
fields.help: What this link does for the book: the meaning, pressure or effect it carries.
